name: Indacaterol
dosing: Inhaled once daily: typically 150–300 mcg OD depending on product
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to indacaterol or formulation excipients; caution in patients with significant cardiovascular disease
interactions: Non-selective beta-blockers may antagonise effect; coadministration with other sympathomimetics may increase cardiovascular side effects; beta2-agonists can lower serum potassium
monitoring: Assess respiratory function (spirometry), heart rate and symptoms; monitor for tremor and palpitations; check serum potassium in at-risk patients
pregnancy: Use in pregnancy only if clearly needed and after specialist discussion
sideEffects: Common: cough, headache, nasopharyngitis, tremor, palpitations; metabolic effects include hypokalaemia
pharmacokinetics: Inhaled with a duration of about 24 hours enabling once-daily dosing
clinicalPearls: Ultra-long-acting LABA suitable for once-daily dosing; always use with an inhaled corticosteroid for asthma control (not as monotherapy); in COPD may be used alone or in combination with LAMA
indication: Maintenance bronchodilator therapy in COPD; adjunctive therapy in asthma only when combined with an inhaled corticosteroid
